Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the ask and propose a short paper trail to secure runway for your Q1 model launch. You indicated an initial steady-state of ~25–30 A100-equivalent GPUs, peaking higher for orthogonal pipelines.

What Redwood is proposing (conditional hold):
- Guaranteed allocation: 20 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for the core inference fleet.
- Soft hold: additional 15 x A100-equivalent reserved as conditional/escrow capacity that we only activate if you pass the final acceptance gate and sign the SOW.
- Hold window: Feb 15, 2027 — May 9, 2027 (12 weeks).
- Next steps: Please confirm the forecast sheet attached and call out any regional constraints (we primarily route your traffic through us-west-2).

If you confirm numbers today, we can provision the conditional escrow agreement and place the soft hold in our provisioning queue (there is a nominal non-refundable hold fee to secure the soft pool; procurement will want details).

I'm copying Hannah and Rishi for ops/technical feasibility checks and Marcus for pricing confirmation.

Putting an ops-read on this thread —

Notes from infra scheduling:
- Fleet snapshot for FebMar 2027 (us-west-2): Planned capacity ~120 x A100-equivalent; ~20 are already committed to existing locked customers during that window. Peak slack looks ~60 GPUs if we don't oversubscribe.
- Risk: We have two large renewals with soft holds overlapping (one in late Jan and another mid-Feb). If both convert, slack reduces to ~25.

Recommendation:
1) Proceed with a split hold: 20 guaranteed + 15 conditional (soft). That matches Runic's ask and buys runway.
2) Put a 10-business-day conversion window for the soft pool and a standard hold fee of $4,500/week for the soft pool (covers opportunity cost and minor provisioning). Fee refundable upon conversion pro-rated; non-refundable otherwise.
3) Create an internal escalation path: if any other conversion pushes slack below safe threshold, we will flag for exec review and propose either temporary burst pricing for the marginal GPUs or an alternate plan using Redwoods quantized-latency pool (lower unit cost but <95% parity depending on model).

Action items: Rishi to validate activation lead times (provisioning + warmup), Marcus to run a quick price delta, Soojin to send the soft-hold agreement to procurement (we'll seed provisional_gpu_escrow_agreement_v1.pdf).

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Dedicated Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Hannah / team —

Technical feasibility/checklist:
- Activation lead time: 7 business days from signed SOW to live endpoint routing for a standard dedicated pool (includes kernel selection, model spin-up for caching warmup, and endpoint verification). If we need custom GPU placement or cross-region peering, add 5 business days.
- Compatibility: Models with 32-bit FP weights will run on A100 native paths; we recommend a mixed strategy if Runic chooses 4-bit quantization for cost-savings (we have benchmarked ~1.9x token cost reduction for some families with <5% quality delta). Provide model names and checkpoints and Ill run the quick profile.
- Mapping: If we provision 35 total (20 guarantee + 15 soft), suggested physical mapping: 5 x 8-GPU DGX-style groups for guaranteed, 2 x 8-GPU groups for soft hold (standby nodes). Soft nodes remain powered but in standby with minimal warmup to save cost; activation moves them into active scheduling.

Attached: provisional_gpu_escrow_agreement_v1.pdf (contains sample hold mechanics and conversion clauses).

I'll join the ops sync Wednesday to run through warmup and KV-cache priming strategy.

-Rishi
